subject: Next steps: model shortlist & bespoke scoring for ZenHealth pilot
summary: Post-demo recap and next steps for ZenHealth pilot: recommended model shortlist, dataset format and scoring rubric for a customer-specific eval on Redwood, cost/latency estimates, and milestones for a two-week pilot. Team to provision transient eval endpoints and share a scoring template for human review.
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Gomez <a.gomez@zenhealth.com>, Kevin Zhou <kevin.zhou@zenhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: model shortlist & bespoke scoring for ZenHealth pilot

Hi Alicia / Kevin —

Thanks again for the demo today — great conversation and lots of alignment on the evaluation goals. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the pilot moving: 

What we heard from your team
- Primary use case: triage summarization + recommended care pathway suggestions for inbound patient messages (safety- and privacy-sensitive).
- Success criteria: > 92% clinical-action alignment on top-1 recommendation (human-reviewed) and median generation latency < 300ms for 512-token contexts.
- Data constraints: subset of de-identified inbound messages (~2k rows) for the first run; ZenHealth will supply a 200-row sample for schema validation.

Redwood recommendation (shortlist) — initial models to evaluate\- RWI-13B-Opt (quantized, 4-bit): balanced quality / cost for classification+summarization tasks\- Llama-2-70b-q4f16 (server-side optimized): higher-quality abstractive summarization, higher cost but better for edge-case language\- Falcon-40B-Instruct (int8): fast generation for templates and short completions

Why these models
- RWI-13B: our tests show consistent top-1 clinical recommendation precision vs. larger models at ~40% lower cost.
- Llama-2-70b: best-in-class abstractive fidelity for ambiguous triage prompts (we recommend it for a second-stage pass).
- Falcon-40B: useful for fast templated responses where latency is critical.

Proposed eval design (what Redwood will run)\- Dataset format: CSV with columns: id, patient_message_text, context_history (optional), gold_recommendation (JSON blob), reviewer_notes\- Split: 200 sample rows to validate schema -> full 2k run for scoring\- Scoring: automated metrics (top-1 match, BLEU for templated text where applicable, embedding-similarity for semantic match) + human reviewer pass with the provided scoring rubric (attached: zenhealth_scoring_template_v1.xlsx)\- Regression guardrails: we’ll compute per-model delta vs. baseline (your current system) and flag any unexpected drops > 3% on primary metric.

Operational asks from ZenHealth
1) Share the 200-row sample by EOD Fri (attach CSV). Please remove PHI — de-identify before upload.
2) Confirm which internal reviewers will do the human scoring (we’ll set reviewer accounts in the Redwood Console).
3) Confirm budget envelope for the pilot so Ben can provision Dedicated vs Hosted eval capacity (we can do a short A/B with dedicated endpoints).

Attachments: zenhealth_eval_dataset_sample.csv (template), redwood_model_recs.pdf, zenhealth_scoring_template_v1.xlsx

If this looks good I’ll loop in Ben to provide cost/latency estimates and Priyom to set up the scoring dashboard and runbooks. Proposed timeline: kickoff validation (sample schema) by Fri, full 2k run starting next Tue, results and human review the following week.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0132

Thanks Vanessa — this is very helpful and matches what we discussed. A few quick clarifications before we push the sample: 

1) For the gold_recommendation JSON blob, can you share an example schema? We have both categorical pathway codes and free-text rationale fields.
2) On the human reviewer side, we have clinicians and ops reviewers. Should we expect separate reviewer labels (clinician_score vs ops_score) in the template?
3) Budget: procurement wants a rough estimate (ballpark) for a two-week pilot on hosted endpoints vs isolated dedicated nodes — can Ben share that number?

Also confirming we will provide the 200-row de-identified sample by Friday. I’ll loop in our clinical lead if you need subject-matter input for scoring.

Best,
Alicia Gomez

Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Next steps: model shortlist & bespoke scoring for ZenHealth pilot

Hi Alicia — quick budget/ops reply and a sample JSON schema for gold_recommendation attached inline. Happy to walk through live if helpful.

Ballpark pilot cost (2 weeks, 2k rows, 3 model variants, hosted streaming):
- Hosted (shared pools): ~$4.5k - $6k (depends on token distribution; includes human review runs)
- Short dedicated burst (reserved GPU for 1 week + hosted fallback): ~$8k - $10k

Latency profile (512-token context)\- RWI-13B-Opt: median 220ms (p50)\- Falcon-40B (int8 path): median 180ms\- Llama-2-70b (q4f16): median 420ms (higher noted in some edge-case prompts)

Operational notes\- We’ll provision ephemeral eval endpoints under the deal id ZH-2026-045; these endpoints can be pinned to model versions and will auto-delete after the pilot.\- Caching: we’ll enable prefix KV caching for repeated context to reduce cost during multi-pass scoring.\- Regression detection: Redwood Optimize will compute deltas and fire an alert if metrics degrade >3% relative to your baseline.

Suggested gold_recommendation JSON schema (example):
{
  "recommendation_code": "string (e.g., PATH-03)",
  "priority": "low|medium|high",
  "recommended_action": "Schedule tele-visit / Refer to specialist / Self-care instructions",
  "confidence_score": "0-1 float",
  "rationale": "string (free text)",
  "source_notes": "list of supporting text ids"
}

On the reviewer labels: yes, please include separate clinician_score and ops_score columns. We’ll surface both in the scorer dashboard and provide weighted aggregation logic (weighting factors editable in the scoring template).

Next steps (ops)
1) Vanessa / Priyom: confirm reviewers and invite them to Redwood Console (we’ll create reviewer accounts).
2) Alicia: share 200-row sample (de-identified) by EOD Fri.
3) Ben: I’ll provision the ephemeral endpoints once we get sign-off on budget envelope; provide a short cost worksheet.

Attachments: inline JSON schema, cost worksheet (attached to thread).

—
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0199
